item.title: 'We play with no fear!' - Mario Hermoso reveals Gian Piero Gasperini's training ground secret after AS Roma halt Paris Saint-Germain's winning streak
item.description: FBL-EUR-C1-PSG-ROMA - AFP Mario Hermoso scored early and earned Player of the Match honours as AS Roma ended Paris Saint-Germain's 100 per cent Champions League start with a 2-2 draw at the Parc des Princes. Speaking afterwards, the Spanish defender explained how Gian Piero Gasperini's fearless system empowers centre-backs to attack. Hermoso inspires fearless Roma to historic Paris point Mario Hermoso set the tone inside five minutes as AS Roma held reigning European champions Paris Saint-Germain to a thrilling 2-2 draw in the first-ever meeting between the clubs on Wednesday night. Winning possession high up the pitch before finishing from Matias Soule's cut-back, the Spanish centre-back helped Gian Piero Gasperini's side end PSG's 100 per cent Champions League start despite goals from Illia Zabarnyi and Ousmane Dembele, with substitute Donyell Malen converting a late penalty after Vitinha's handball. "Everyone knows what the coach does, this is his identity, his style of playing," Hermoso told Sky Sport Italia after collecting UEFA's Player of the Match award. "We defenders get the opportunity to be protagonists, so I am very happy to come to a stadium like this, and see Roma playing in this special way, with no fear. We are on the right track and must keep taking these big steps forward." Training ground drills and Gasperini's squad rotation Gasperini sprang a tactical surprise by leaving Malen, Paulo Dybala and Bryan Cristante on the bench from the start, yet Roma's rotated line-up matched the French giants across 90 minutes. Hermoso, who also went close to adding a second open-play goal, revealed how attacking rotations are rehearsed daily. "With these team-mates who play in attack, we do try to make these moves in training sessions, everyone gets to have a go, and that means us defenders can bring something extra to the team, it's an added benefit," he explained. Addressing the bench impact, Hermoso added: "Everyone in this squad is important, we are set out in a way that we can all be protagonists. Dony, Paulo and Bryan had more minutes in this season, but they came on with the right mentality, and were ready to help get a good result." Building a winning mentality against European champions PSG only breached Roma's open-play organisation through Zabarnyi's 31st-minute corner header and Dembele's 62nd-minute spot-kick after Achraf Hakimi was fouled by Wesley. Hermoso credited Gasperini with transforming Roma's resilience in high-pressure European fixtures. "The coach gives you confidence to believe, to have this mentality of reacting to difficult moments that we suffered not just this season, but over the years," Hermoso told Prime Video . "This is important, given the way the team came in, the way we played this match against a team that has won the last two Champions Leagues. The result is a huge achievement... item.title: Botham back as Morgan-Williams to make first start
item.description: James Botham and Reuben Morgan-Williams were part of the Wales squad that beat New Zealand [Getty Images/Huw Evans Picture Agency] Wales flanker James Botham has been recalled by head coach Steve Tandy as one of five changes for the Nations Championship finale against Japan at the Allianz Stadium on Saturday. In the only backline alteration for the game in Twickenham, Ospreys scrum-half Reuben Morgan-Williams will make his first Wales start, with Tomos Williams named among the replacements. Exeter lock Dafydd Jenkins will captain the side for the first time in more than two years with regular skipper Dewi Lake and flanker Jac Morgan also dropping to the bench. Prop Rhys Carre and hooker Ryan Elias make their first starts of the November campaign, while lock Adam Beard returns at the expense of Ben Carter. Botham back after missing out on Australia James Botham is the grandson of England cricket legend Lord Botham [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Botham produced a player-of-the-match display in the 35-28 victory against New Zealand after making 30 tackles but was left out of the 29-26 defeat by Australia in favour of Cardiff colleague Alex Mann. It was a decision which Botham’s father Liam, himself a former Cardiff wing, said Tandy had got wrong. “I know there's a lot been spoken about it,” said Tandy. “Everyone has got their opinions and people generally tell you who should be in the team and they never tell you who shouldn't. “We're a tight group and as a coach I make sure I speak to all the players before if they are not selected. There'll be reasons why, whether it be bigger picture or whether it is form. “I'll always speak to those, that's a special thing and the connection we feel in our environment.” Botham, who became a father earlier this week, will play at open-side flanker against Japan after starring at blind-side against the All Blacks, with Mann and number eight Aaron Wainwright completing the back row. “James was outstanding against the All Blacks, but we've got a back row depth there that we can move things around and freshen things up," said Tandy. “James has had his little one, he's coming back in full of energy. item.title: Major MLS playoff overhaul confirmed as league axes wild card round and best-of-three series
item.description: Inter Miami CF v D.C. United - Getty Images Sport Major League Soccer (MLS) is finalising another major overhaul of its post-season format, with the wild card round and best-of-three first round set to be scrapped from the 2027-28 campaign. The revamped 16-team structure aims to boost regular-season intensity after the current format proved ineffective at sustaining momentum and rewarding the league's top performers. MLS set for major play-off overhaul MLS is finalising another major overhaul of its post-season structure , even as the 2026 MLS Cup play-offs get under way. Beginning with the 2027-28 season, the league will eliminate its short-lived wild card round and scrap the best-of-three first-round format, according to reports from The Guardian . The changes will condense the play-off field to 16 teams. Under the new model, the opening two rounds will be played as two-legged, home-and-away ties, while the semi-finals and final will revert to single-elimination matches hosted by the higher seed. Why the league is scrapping best-of-three Introduced in 2023, the best-of-three opening round has proved ineffective at sustaining drama or rewarding regular-season excellence. Over the past three campaigns, a staggering 35 days elapsed between the end of the regular season and the second round due to the November international break. While the 2026 World Cup break allowed MLS to push the start of this year's play-offs past the international window, the gap from Decision Day to the quarter-finals still stretched to 28 days. The league had also weighed an Australian rules football-inspired double-elimination model before settling on its latest plan. Although an MLS spokesperson did not immediately comment on the latest reports, the league confirmed its review back in August. "Major League Soccer is continuing to evaluate potential adjustments to its postseason format as part of a broader review of the league’s shift to a new competition calendar, beginning with the 2027-28 season," a spokesperson said at the time. A bid to restore regular-season intensity A primary driver behind the constant adjustments is the desire to raise the stakes of the regular season. Currently, 60 per cent of clubs qualify for the play-offs, creating an overly forgiving race. That leniency was highlighted this year when Real Salt Lake reached the first round despite winning just once in 16 matches after the World Cup. They edged out Minnesota United on Decision Day, even though Minnesota had endured a run of one victory in 18 games. The 2027-28 model will become the sixth different play-off format MLS has used since its 1996 launch. The league briefly abandoned multi-legged ties in 2019 before reintroducing extended series following its broadcast partnership with Apple, partly to guarantee lower-ranked qualifiers at least one match of post-season revenue. The former NBA player had plenty of praise for the young forward after the Portland Trail Blazers beat the San Antonio Spurs 116-111 in NBA Cup group-stage action on Wednesday night. item.title: Exeter not 'the finished article', says boss Taylor
item.description: Matt Taylor has seen his side lose just one of their past 10 games in all competitions - away at League Two leaders Salford City [Shutterstock] Exeter City are "nowhere near the finished article" despite their recent upturn in form, manager Matt Taylor has said. Having been a point above the relegation places at the end of September, Exeter have become one of League Two's in-form teams. They have lost just one of their past 10 matches in all competitions, keeping clean sheets in half of those games. It has seen them rise to eighth in the division and also book an FA Cup second round tie after winning at then League One leaders Huddersfield Town in the first round. "The last 10 games now has been a period of games where we lost one, and that was as good a performance as we've had all season at Salford against a very strong opposition, incredible cup results and good league form," Taylor told BBC Radio Devon. "So we're going in the right direction, but nowhere near the finished article. "We'll constantly have challenges in-game and in the lead-up to games with the way we are as a group in terms of real depth and experience. "But in terms of the strides and the progress I think individuals have made within the team in that period I'm speaking about, I think you can see players are performing to a better level and with a bigger output and a bigger influence on the game. "I've always said I'll sleep well at night as long as the group is honest with me. "I feel this is a really honest group, but I'm still as excited as ever to see where it could take us in two weeks' time, in two months' time, in two years' time for some of them, but certainly as this season goes deeper seeing where we're at." Exeter defender Harper 'honoured' by Kenya cap Taylor impressed with Exeter City's Oldham comeback Exeter host a resurgent Crawley Town on Saturday (12:30 GMT) with the joint-second best home record in League Two. They have conceded just twice in eight games at St James Park, winning five and drawing the other three. It is a record that Taylor is proud of, having won their past four home games. "There's certain records we're really proud of this season: our defensive record, clean sheets, our home record, our home form," added Taylor. "Even more so because it connects the team with the fans. You want a strong home showing. "Very rarely this season do I think our home fans have gone home disappointed or frustrated with what they've seen and that's the majority of our fan base, that's where they get to see us, close to home, less travel involved. "Also, we have to take into account how far opposition teams have to travel down to us, same for us when we go to Oldham and Crawley, all these teams away from home, not just the north but London-based as well. This isn't an easy place to come to but we've got to make sure our energy is in the right place on Saturday." All the latest Exeter City news

item.title: 19 Hillsdale County volleyball athletes earn all-league SCAA-East
item.description: ILLSDALE COUNTY — Hillsdale County volleyball programs dominated the Southern Central Athletic Association East Division postseason honors following the 2026 fall sports season, accounting for all four Dream Team selections and 19 all-conference honorees. Hillsdale Academy seniors Lucy Cote and Malorie-Kate Apel and Pittsford juniors Alexis Bryner and Karmin Butler earned SCAA Dream Team honors, while Pittsford head coach Jessica Butler was named the division’s coach of the year. Butler led the Wildcats to a 21-12 overall record, their best finish since 2022, and an appearance in the Division 4 district championship game. Bryner, Cote and Apel also earned all-region honors from the Michigan Interscholastic Volleyball Coaches Association this fall. Hillsdale Academy earned six all-conference selections after finishing the season 23-9 and capturing its fourth consecutive district championship along with the division crown. Joining Cote and Apel with first-team honors was fellow senior Zoe Plemmons. Camden-Frontier junior Zailey Conroy rounded out Hillsdale County’s first-team selections. Local athletes accounted for six of the seven first-team honorees. Five more Hillsdale County athletes earned second-team honors, including Pittsford freshman Layla Bryner and sophomore Ellie Bump, Hillsdale Academy junior Abigail Kriesch and freshman Lucy Molenkamp and Camden-Frontier junior Alyssa Schroeder. Litchfield, Waldron and North Adams-Jerome were also represented among the honorable mention selections, with all six Hillsdale County programs competing in the division earning postseason recognition. item.title: Oliver Bearman locks in Haas F1 seat as 2027 grid officially set
item.description: Motorsport photo Oliver Bearman will officially stay at Haas for the 2027 F1 season after he and the team finally put pen to paper on a new deal. On Thursday Haas announced Bearman would stay put for next year, partnering Brazilian rookie Rafael Camara at the squad. Nico Hulkenberg, Audi F1 Team, Oliver Bearman, Haas F1 Team Nico Hulkenberg, Audi F1 Team, Oliver Bearman, Haas F1 Team Ferrari protege Bearman was always going to stay with the US-owned team, which has had him on loan from the Scuderia for the past two seasons. But as he is set for his third year with the squad, Bearman's camp also wanted some assurances about his long-term future. And having become Haas' lead driver over the past two years, outperforming the now ousted Esteban Ocon and partnering a rookie in Camara next year, Bearman's camp is also believed to look for a significant pay increase. item.title: Barcelona may have found their defensive answers in La Masia starlet – report
item.description: Barcelona may have found their defensive answers in La Masia starlet – report Barcelona extended their winning run to five matches in all competitions following a 4-1 win over Sabah in the UEFA Champions League. Apart from the stellar attacking display, a key highlight of the night was the debut of La Masia starlet Alex Campos. The young defender came in as a 64th minute replacement for Frenkie de Jong and had a solid enough outing. An answer to Barcelona’s defensive problems? Alex Campos made his debut against Sabah. (Picture credit: X/@FCBarcelona) It is no secret that Barcelona are struggling defensively. Even Hansi Flick looked visibly frustrated after the team conceded a goal against Sabah. The team simply lacks enough depth in central defence. But as reported by Diario SPORT , Flick may have found his answer in the form of Campos. With Andreas Christensen still struggling with injuries, Pau Cubarsi carrying a knock and the likes of Eric Garcia and Jules Kounde often required elsewhere, Barcelona have been crying out for a reliable centre-back. De Jong has done well to chip in, but he is not a natural in this position, leaving Flick with Gerard Martin as the only other option. Campos’ cameo in Baku may prove to be a first step towards him becoming a real alternative for Barcelona. The report frames the youngster as a potential example of Barcleona solving the defensive problem from within. The Catalans have a solid track record of doing so, having previously solved multiple problems for giving chances to academy players such as Marc Casado, Marc Bernal, Fermin Lopez and Cubarsi himself. What does Campos bring to the table? Campos is rated highly by Bojan. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) As far as his profile is concerned, Campos is quite similar to Cubarsi. Originally a midfielder before Barcelona converted him into a central defender, Campos’ natural qualities include playing out from the back and the ability to join attacks. He is also a genuine threat from set-pieces and is very efficient on the ball. Under Juliano Belletti, however, his defensive game has improved enormously and he is now regarded as a solid, reliable operator in central defence. Campos is also quite versatile, as he can perform both as a left and a right sided centre-back. He is comfortable filling in as a holding midfielder as well. Perhaps more importantly, Campos rarely loses his composure. He is already held in high regard by the likes of Bojan Krkic and Belletti and it will be interesting to see if he is used more often by Flick in the coming weeks.

item.title: Jose Mourinho identifies key issue with Real Madrid’s squad players after PSV scare
item.description: Jose Mourinho identifies key issue with Real Madrid’s squad players after PSV scare Real Madrid have secured ten successive wins in all competitions and are looking like the team to beat at the moment. However, the team is not without its faults, and it was evident in the first half of their game against PSV Eindhoven in the UEFA Champions League. The defensive duo of Antonio Rudiger and Eder Militao looked completely out of sorts , prompting Jose Mourinho to make changes in the second half. Mourinho identifies a key issue Mourinho wants more quality from his second squad. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) As reported by Defensa Central , Mourinho believes that his rotation options are simply not performing as expected. The Real Madrid coach has observed that when the fringe players come in, Real Madrid often lose their brightness and competitive edge. It is a pattern that Mourinho has noticed on multiple occasions, with the likes of Rudiger, Trent Alexander-Arnold, Alvaro Carreras and Eduardo Camavinga often failing to perform to the expected level. These players have lacked the quality and the consistency the first-choice XI has provided this season, and the 5-1 win over PSV was the latest example. Mourinho made six changes to the starting lineup, but the team struggled in the first half and conceded. He had experienced similar situations in the comebacks against Celta Vigo and AEK Athens. A necessary balancing act Mourinho is using Luis Enrique’s playbook. (Photo by Clive Brunskill/Getty Images) Despite this shortcoming from lesser-used players, Mourinho remains committed to using the full depth of his squad. The Portuguese is working on managing a demanding schedule in December through a selection rest plan. He is determined to keep his first-choice players fresh for key matches. item.title: Joshua Zirkzee makes his position unmistakable after Man United’s controversy-filled Sporting encounter
item.description: Joshua Zirkzee makes his position unmistakable after Man United’s controversy-filled Sporting encounter Joshua Zirkzee has made his feelings crystal clear after Manchester United’s controversy-filled 2-2 Champions League draw against Sporting CP. Controversy Pochettino was denied his first win as United head coach, with multiple bizarre refereeing decisions going against him and his players. Referee Szymon Marciniak ruled out an Amad Diallo goal during the second half, having adjudged Youri Tielemans to have committed a foul in the build-up. Marciniak’s whistle came just before Amad found the net, ruling out any VAR intervention. The Polish referee compounded matters by awarding Sporting a debatable first-half penalty and disallowing what would have been a late United winner for a push on goalkeeper Kaique Pereira. The decision to chalk off United’s goal seemed baffling given that he allowed a similar Suárez goal to stand when there was slight contact with Senne Lammens . Pochettino hit out at the decisions in his post-match remarks to reporters , but he chose to emphasise the positives and the fine attitude his players displayed. In an interview with MUTV , Zirkzee acknowledged how costly the referee’s shocking performance had been, but insisted it was solely down to him and his teammates to deliver the victory. Zirkzee’s verdict The Dutchman told club media, “In my opinion, there were definitely some key decisions there that didn’t really favour us. We shouldn’t look at the referee, we should look at ourselves instead, but it definitely has an impact on us, you can’t deny that.” “But the team that we have, we should come here and not look at the ref and make sure that we get the win, regardless of the decisions that he makes.” He continued, “Obviously, we did come here to win, so in a way, we’ve got some positives to take.” “But with our recent form, of course, we’re disappointed to not win. Some positives to take, we’ve just got to keep moving forward, keep going together, keep putting in the work and move onto the next game.” Zirkzee said of his return to the starting XI, “I’m very happy; every game you play for this club is an honour. I’ve been here for some time and it’s been a while since I started a game, so I’m very happy, I just wish we could have got a win.” “For where we’re standing at right now, to have a fanbase like that is just incredible. All we can do is get up the next day and make sure the next time they travel with us and the next time they watch our game, we repay it, so that’s all we can do for now.” Looking ahead to Saturday’s meeting with Brentford, Zirkzee remarked, “It’s a big test. The fans deserve a result and all we want is a result. We’ve got to dig ourselves out of the trenches.” United sit in 19th place in the Premier League table heading into the game against Brentford.

After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
